item.title: Flying Fijians must stay disciplined and connected for full 80 minutes - Seruvakula
item.description: The FIJI Water Flying Fijians will need to be disciplined on both sides of the ball, and stay connected for the full 80 minutes as they prepare to take on Canada tonight. Those were the words of Interim Coach Senirusi Seruvakula from Japan, saying that they will never underestimate Canada as they are a very good side.
item.content:encoded:
The FIJI Water Flying Fijians will need to be disciplined on both sides of the ball, and stay connected for the full 80 minutes as they prepare to take on Canada tonight.

Those were the words of Interim Coach Senirusi Seruvakula from Japan, saying that they will never underestimate Canada as they are a very good side.

Seruvakula says Canada has an advantage over them as they played Japan last weekend.

He says they currently have no injuries in the squad and are looking forward to tonight's game.

Skipper Tevita Ikanivere says they have had a great preparation for the past two weeks, and the boys are excited to play Canada tonight.

Ikanivere also mentioned that they have four debutants for this game in No. 8 Isoa Tuwai, Penaia Cakobau, Inoke Ravuiwasa and Terio Tamani.

The Flying Fijians are the current defending Asahi Super Dry Pacific Nations Cup champions.

Fiji will take on Canada at 7 tonight in Osaka.

Meanwhile, Japan will meet the USA at 10pm.

item.title: Food, memories and sisterhood at SJSS Pacific Market Day
item.description: The spirit of sisterhood was on full display today as Saint Joseph’s Secondary School alumnae gathered for a Pacific Market Day featuring food, handicrafts, island wear and entertainment. The SJSS Alumnae Pacific Market Day was held at the school hall as part of the school’s 70th anniversary celebrations, bringing together former students, current students, families and supporters.
item.content:encoded:
The spirit of sisterhood was on full display today as Saint Joseph’s Secondary School alumnae gathered for a Pacific Market Day featuring food, handicrafts, island wear and entertainment.

The SJSS Alumnae Pacific Market Day was held at the school hall as part of the school’s 70th anniversary celebrations, bringing together former students, current students, families and supporters.

The event provided an opportunity for alumnae to reconnect with old friends and share memories from their years at the school.

Among those running a stall was Roslyn Lee, a member of the Class of 1976 and President of the SJSS Alumnae in Australia.

Lee says it is wonderful to return to Fiji and reconnect with friends she has not seen for many years.

INSERT: Lee on reconnecting with friends 12th Sept

The Australian alumnae also supported the Market Day through the “Aussie Lucky Dip”, with items available for $5 and $10.

Lee thanked alumnae in Australia for donating items and local Fiji-based alumnae for coming out to support the initiative.

S he is encouraging SJSS alumnae living in Australia to get in touch and stay connected.

Lee also reminded current students that the alumnae are there to support them and encouraged them to give back to their communities once they leave school.

The 70th anniversary celebrations will conclude tonight with the Pacific Elegance Ball, which will begin at 6pm at the Vodafone Arena.

item.title: 7 jobs created after opening of new restaurant in Labasa
item.description: Karishma Kumari , Mohammed Feroz · 12/09/2026 Seven new jobs have been created following the opening of the Fry Master Restaurant in Tuatua, Labasa, as the business looks to meet growing demand for dining options outside Labasa Town.
item.content:encoded:
Karishma Kumari , Mohammed Feroz · 12/09/2026

Seven new jobs have been created following the opening of the Fry Master Restaurant in Tuatua, Labasa, as the business looks to meet growing demand for dining options outside Labasa Town.

Restaurant owner Ashneel Sharma says the decision to open the restaurant in Tuatua was driven by high demand from customers, particularly those travelling between Labasa and Savusavu who have limited restaurant options outside Labasa Town.

Sharma says traffic congestion and limited parking in Labasa also made it difficult for customers to access restaurants in the town area.

He says locating Fry Master outside the Labasa Town boundary provides customers with another option that is easier to access.

Sharma says affordability is also a key focus of the business, with the restaurant aiming to keep its food prices lower compared to other restaurants and to provide delivery services to customers within a 10-kilometre radius.

He adds finding a suitable location was one of the biggest challenges he faced while trying to establish the restaurant.

He says despite this initial difficulty, he remained determined to establish the business.

item.title: Three-month-old Marina given new hope after heart treatment in Fiji
item.description: Marina was discharged from the Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Children’s Hospital, after receiving treatment for a heart condition that was discovered shortly after birth. She was among three children discharged from the Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Children’s Hospital after receiving treatment for heart conditions.
item.content:encoded:
Marina was discharged from the Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Children’s Hospital, after receiving treatment for a heart condition that was discovered shortly after birth.

She was among three children discharged from the Sri Sathya Sai Sanjeevani Children’s Hospital after receiving treatment for heart conditions.

Tirii says the family did not know Marina had a heart condition at birth, but doctors detected a heart murmur after she became sick during her first week of life.

Further tests later confirmed that Marina had a large ventricular septal defect, or VSD, which is a hole in the heart.

Tirii says finding out that her first child had a heart condition was difficult and unexpected.

Marina continued to receive medical check-ups in the Solomon Islands before arrangements were made for the mother and daughter to travel to Fiji for treatment.

Tirii says travelling away from home with her three-month-old baby was not easy, but she is grateful her daughter was able to receive the care she needed.

She has thanked the Solomon Islands Government for supporting their journey to Fiji, as well as the surgeons, donors and medical teams involved in Marina’s care.

After the uncertainty surrounding her daughter’s condition and the journey away from home for treatment, Tirii is now grateful to be leaving hospital with Marina and looking forward to taking her home.
